documents.title: Quoting Daniel Stenberg
documents.summary: During the time these agents converted 185,000 lines of C code into 340,000 lines of Rust code (I counted), we merged over 300 commits in the actual curl project. We actually improved curl during these a little more than three weeks. A little over 200 bugfixes actually. 200 bugfixes that none of those rust rewrites have. We also fixed a few vulnerabilities. In another month we have done another 200 and maybe fixed a few more vulnerabilities. Will these clones keep up? — Daniel Stenberg , Actual curl rewrites in Rust Tags: daniel-stenberg , curl , rust , security , coding-agents , c , ai , llms , generative-ai , vibe-porting

documents.title: The PSF end-of-year fundraiser
documents.summary: The PSF end-of-year fundraiser With my Python Software Foundation board director hat on: we've launched our end-of-year fundraiser for the non-profit that supports Python development and the Python community. If your company or your work benefits from Python, please consider donating this year! The PSF looks after the IP behind Python, operates PyPI, sponsors core developer sprints, supports community events (including running PyCon US every year), and employs a small and excellent staff team to keep everything running. We also operate the Developers in Residence program , which now includes three security developers (welcome, Brett Smith) focused on helping secure Python, PyPI, and the wider ecosystem. Tags: python , psf
